message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra.  
Their most recent common ancestor was a small, insectivorous‑to‑omnivorous mammal that lived in the Paleocene epoch, roughly 60 million years ago. This ancestor was a member of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, the group that gave rise to many modern placental mammals such as bats, cetaceans, even‑toed ungulates, odd‑toed ungulates, and carnivores.  

Because it is extinct and only known from the fossil record and phylogenetic inference, it does not have a formal species name; it is simply referred to as the “last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla” (or of lions and zebras).
